From the Principal’s Desk

         Dear Students! I heartily welcome you all to pursue higher education at Raha College
for the academic session 2025-2026. Raha College has a rich history of 60 years and this year,
the college will be celebrating its diamond jubilee in the later part of the year. Raha College has
been imparting higher education to the poor, needy and socially disadvantaged group of
students of Raha and its adjoining areas. Our vision is to serve the social needs and to uplift the
living standards of the rural youths by imparting higher education and fostering an enduring
sense of discipline and single minded dedication to work. Our objective is to help students
realize their true potential so that they can face the challenges of life.

Raha College, established in 1964, is the only degree college in Raha constituency offering
degree course in Arts, Science and Commerce streams and is permanently affiliated to Gauhati
University (GU). NEP 2020 (FYUGP-GU) has been introduced in the college from the academic
session 2023-24. Besides, the college has two distance education study centers: Krishna Kanta
Handique Open State University (KKHSOU) offering graduate, post graduate degrees along
with diplomas and certificate courses and Assam State Open School (ASOS) offering higher
secondary level course in Arts stream. The college also offers Higher Secondary course under
Assam State School Education Board Division –II (Erstwhile AHSEC) in the Arts stream. Our
college takes pride in being a place, where students can pursue knowledge at their own pace,
aided by the rich faculty members, who guide them at every step. We strive to establish a vibrant
learning environment that would expand the horizon of knowledge and skill. The concept of
quality education has become a common feature of higher education in India and abroad.
Keeping in pace with changing times, we have constructed modern digital classrooms,
conference room, new science laboratories, new academic building, fully acoustic auditorium,
computer lab, modern gym and renovated classrooms. We are thankful to RUSA and UGC for
providing us financial support to construct new infrastructure in the college premises. During
the pandemic phase, we provided online classes to our students and every department of the
institute conducted webinars, which were attended not only by the faculty and students of our
college but also by teachers and students from different colleges and universities of the country.
Raha College is conducting seminars, faculty improvement programs, teacher exchange
programs, regular field visits by students and teachers, invited speakers from reputed institutes
in order to enrich the academic ambience. The college also provides ample opportunities to the
students to develop themselves in co-curricular activities and sports.

 The college also conducts national seminars, conferences and debate competitions and is
engaged in the work of dissemination of knowledge. In today’s world of cut-throat competition,
it is essential to be equipped with appropriate knowledge, communication skills, values and the
right attitude to become successful in life. A holistic development is the only answer to tide over
the emerging challenges and difficulties posed by the uncertainties of the present time.
Discipline and hard work is the key to success along with ambition and defining one’s goals
clearly. The future belongs to you; your need therefore, is to prepare yourself for an active
participation in life. I, on behalf of Raha College family welcome all aspiring students to this
college to scale new heights of success and achieve greater glory.

                                                                    With warm wishes
                                                                 Dr. Beda Kumar Chaliha

                                  Foreword

         Raha College provides the ideal ambience for students having a desire to pursue higher
education in Three-year Degree course in the streams of Arts, Science and Commerce. The
College introduced Science and Commerce stream from the academic session 2016-17. Set
amidst the meadows and lush green foliage of resplendent trees , in a serene atmosphere within
the town, the College offers an ideal location for teaching-learning ambits. It is located at a
distance of one and half K.M. from Raha town Natun Chariali and can be approached from
three main roads. It is only at a distance of 400 meter from the junction of NH-37 road toward
Chaparmukh Railway junction. This seat of higher learning is preparing to celebrated its
Diamond Jubilee this year. The College was accredited “B” grade in its third cycle of NAAC
quality assessment in October 2023. The College has two distance education centers at present
functioning under Krishna Kanta Handique State Open University, offering BA and MA
programmes, and Assam State Open School (ASOS) offering Higher Secondary level course in
Arts stream.
         The dream of setting up a seat of higher learning was achieved through the endeavor,
zeal and aspiration of some far-sighted and enlightened social activists of greater Raha area,
and it turned into a reality with the establishment of the College on 28th July 1964. Till date,
Raha College is the only general degree college in Raha Legislative Assembly Constituency
reserved for Scheduled Caste. The College is permanently affiliated to Gauhati University.
Apart from the regular degree course, the College also runs the HS course in Arts as per
AHSEC curriculum. The College has rich faculty members, a modern library and a Computer
Centre. It is worth mentioning that the teaching-learning process has received a fillip with the
introduction of state of art digital class rooms constructed with the financial assistance received
from the Govt. of Assam. Under RUSA Grant, new infrastructure like the new academic
building, renovated acoustic auditorium, cycle stand, Science laboratory, renovated classrooms,
etc, have been set up.

Goals and Objectives of the College

         Raha College started its mission with zeal to promote higher education to the largely
underdeveloped people of Raha locality since its inception in 1964. The mission of the College is
to serve the rural youths by providing them with easy access to higher education and job
opportunities. The College will strive towards integrated personality, growth of rural students in
particular and students at large in which special attention is given to their intellectual, moral
and cultural development. Another important objective of the College is to inculcate the spirit of
inquisitiveness among the students and to instill in them the spirit of patriotism, dedication and
humanistic values.

Vision
        The vision of the College is to make it a seat of excellence and to uplift the living
standards of the rural youths by imparting them higher education and fostering an enduring
sense of discipline and single-minded dedication to their work.

INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT

    The college is endowed with excellent physical infrastructural facilities to support the
teaching –learning process. The main campus is spread over 6.48 acres. The college has a
spacious seminar/conference hall. There are adequate numbers of classrooms, separate
departments, and separate departmental class rooms to facilitate the academic programmes.
The infrastructure involves spacious class rooms, proper lighting and ventilation, seating
arrangement with proper visibility for both students and teachers. There are common rooms for
boys and girls separately. There is a special arrangement for canteen for students and staff, and
there is an auditorium cum indoor stadium. The college has hostel facility for boys and a girl’s
hostel is being constructed. The details of the facilities available with the institution are as
under.
    1. Technology Enabled Learning Facility: The College has eight ICT Classrooms where
         the provision of multimedia Projectors, Multimedia Learning, Wi-Fi Connectivity is
         available. A new computer lab with 25 computers has been set up. The institute has set
         up a 25KVA eco-friendly silent generator for power backup to the campus during
         electric failure.
    2. Conference Hall: The College has one modern conference hall and it is regularly used
         for conducting meetings, group discussions, etc.
    3. Seminar Hall: The College has two seminar hall with a seating capacity of 100 and 50
         respectively. Seminar halls are equipped with LCD screen and multimedia projector.
    4. Laboratories: The College has two laboratories in the Arts stream, one in Education
         department and the other in Geography department for conduct of practical classes
         during the session and in annual examination. New modern Science laboratories in all
         the science subjects available in our college have been set up. The college received
         funds from RUSA for construction of science laboratories.
    5. Library Facility: Raha College Central library has more than 28,000 books which
         include text books, reference books, journals; magazines etc. The library remains open
         on all working days from 9.00 AM to 4.00 PM. Photostat facility is available at a
         nominal rate for students of the college. A student is provided with a card with the
         facility to borrow two books at a time for 15 days. A major or honors student gets the
         privilege for borrowing 4 books at a time. Students are to follow library rules. State of
         the art Digital Library is another important feature of the library
    6. Hostel Facility: The College has one Boy’s Hostel and Girls’ Hostel within the college
         Campus. The number of seats available in the Boys Hostel is 18 and in the Girl’s Hostel
         is 22. Hostel seats are allotted at the time of admission on the basis of merit.
    7. Canteen Facility: The College has a canteen in the campus. Students can have
         refreshment in the canteen during the college hour.
    8. Sports Facility: The College has always created a niche for itself in the field of sports.
         In sports, the college provides indoor and outdoor games.

    9. Outdoor Games: A Spacious 2 acre play ground is available for outdoor games i.e.,
       cricket, football, athletics etc. in the college campus. There are separate volleyball and
       badminton courts in the campus. A practicing ground with nets for cricketers has been
       set up separately.
                                                                                        P age |5


    10. Indoor Games: Facilities for sports like Table Tennis, Chess, multi-gym, Carom, etc,
        are available to students. Gym facilities for both students and staff are available in tune
        with the Fit India initiative.
    11. Auditorium cum Indoor Stadium: The College has a modern and state of art acoustic
        auditorium. The seating capacity of the auditorium is around 600.
    12. Class Rooms: All the departments have their individual classrooms for taking
        major/honors classes. Besides, there are sufficient classrooms, some of them renovated
        recently through RUSA funds to facilitate students in their learning.
    13. Departmental Rooms: The departments have been provided with individual rooms so
        that teachers can plan their classes and other related educational and co-curricular
        activities.
    14. Disabled friendly, barrier free environment: There is ramp provision with built
        environment and one disabled –friendly washroom in the campus.
    15. CCTV Surveillance: The college campus and hostel are secured by 24x7 CCTV
        surveillance.
    16. Girls’ Common Room: The College has a facility of girls’ common room with a seating
        capacity of 80 students. The common room has attached toilet with sanitary napkin
        unending machine and incineration.
    17. Green campus initiatives of the college includes the following: Pedestrian friendly
        pathways, landscaping with trees and plants, ban on use of plastic, no tobacco zone,
        restricted entry of automobiles in the college campus. Raha College received “ Green
        and Clean Award 2020” from Anti-Global Warming Society. Morigaon in 2021.

          with effect from the academic session 2024-2025 in the State universities, Deemed to be

          Institutions of higher learning that offers UG, PG and Ph. D. programmes, the
affiliating

          develop synergy among affiliated colleges for holistic implementation of the policy.
Each of
          the Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) will integrate its academic plans ranging from

Structure of Year, Semester, Term:

An academic year is divided into two semesters. There shall also be a special Summer
Term. A semester consists of approximately 90 working days

One working week will have approximately 40 hours of instructional time.

 A Summer term is for eight weeks/two months from 01june -31July. Summer
term courses may be offered on a fast-track mode to enable students to complete
arrears/special courses.

(Note: Teachers can avail the summer vacation from 15 June-15July, devoting the
first part of June for evaluation and the last part of July for preparatory work for
the next academic session)

The HEI can decide on the kind of courses to be offered in the summer term,
based on the requirements and also based on the availability of teaching faculty.

Internship/apprenticeship can be carried out during the summer term,
mandatorily for student who exit after two semesters or four semesters of study
in addition to the skill based courses

Semesters 1 and 2:

The aim of these courses is to develop an understanding in all major arcas
of learning such as the Natural Sciences, Social Sciences, Humanities,
Mathematical and computational thinking and analysis, creative
expressions, and vocational education. The courses will be broad in scope,
and introductory in nature.

In addition, students will also take courses in the Ability Enhancement
(AEQ), Skill Enhancement (SEC) and Value Added (VAC) categories

Semester 3 and 4:
Students will choose courses of their interest in major and minor
They will also pursue courses to strengthen their language skills and other
skill augmenting courses/ vocational training

Semester 5 and 6:
 Higher level courses on the chosen Major and/or Minor in the
disciplinary /interdisciplinary areas of learning in order to gain in-depth
knowledge.

Students will also undertake vocational courses to gain work related skills

Semester 7 and 8:
Advance level courses in Major/Minor disciplines, along with Research
Methodology, for UG degree with Honours.

For Honours with Research UG degree, course content will include
advance level courses, research methodology and Research Project.
Students may be allowed to carry out a research project or dissertation in
another department of the same institution or another institution
equipped with required facilities

Programmes of study

UG Degree Programmes with Single Major:
A student has to secure a minimum of 50% credits from the major discipline for the 3-
year/4-year UG degree to be awarded a single major. For example, in a 3-year UG
programme, if the total number of credits to be carned is 120, a student of Physics with a
minimum of 60 credits will be awarded a B.Sc. in Physics with a single major. Similarly,
in a 4-year UG programme, if the total number of credits to be carned is 160, a student of
Physics with a minimum of 80 credits will be awarded a B.Sc. (Hlons./Ion. With
Research) in Physics in a 4-year UG programme with single major.


UG Degree Programmes with Double Major:
A student has to secure a minimum of 40% credits from the second major discipline for
the 3-year/ 4-year UG degree to be awarded a double major. For example, in a 3-year UG
programme, if the total number of credits to be earned is 120, a student of Physics with a
minimum of 48 credits will be awarded a B.Sc. in Physics with a double major. Similarly,
in a 4-year UG programme, if the total number of credits to be earned is 160, a student of
Physics with a minimum of 64 credits will be awarded a B.Sc. (ITons./Ilon. with
Research) in Physics in a 4-year UG programme with double major.

Interdisciplinary UG Programmes:
The credits for core courses shall be distributed among the constituent
disciplines /subjects so as to get core competence in the interdisciplinary programme.
For example, a degree in Econometrics requires courses in economics, statistics, and
mathematics. The total credits to core courses shall be distributed so that the student
gets full competence in Econometrics upon completion of the programme. The degree
for such students will be awarded as B.Sc. in Econometrics for a 3-year UG programme
or B.Sc. (Honours) / B.Sc. (Honours with Research) in Econometrics for a 4-year UC
programme.

Multidisciplinary UG Programmes:
In the case of students pursuing a multidisciplinary programme of study, the credits to
core courses will be distributed among the broad disciplines such as Life sciences,
Physical Sciences, Mathematical and Computer Sciences, Data Analysis, Social Science
Humanities, etc, For example, a student who opts for a UG program in Life sciences
have the total credits to core courses distributed across Botany, Zoology and
biology disciplines. The degree will be awarded as B.Sc. in Life Sciences programme and B.Sc.
(Honours) in Life Sciences or B.Sc. (Honours with Research) for a
4-year programme without or with a rescarch component respectively.

Note:
The statutory bodies of the Universities and Colleges such as the Board of Studies and
Academic Council will decide on the list of courses under major category and credit
distribution for double major, interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary programmes.

Duration of the Programme:

The duration of the UG programme is 4 years or 8 semesters. Students who desire to
Undergo a 3-year UG Programme will be allowed to exit after completion of the 3rd
year. Students who exit with a UG certificate or UG diploma are permitted to re-enter within
three years and complete the degree programme. Students may be permitted to take a break
from the study during the period of study but the total duration for completing the programme
shall not exceed 7 years.

Credit hours for different types of courses
        The workload relating to a course is measured in terms of credit hours. A credit is a unit
by which the coursework is measured. Tt determines the number of hours of instruction
required per week over the duration of a semester (minimum 15 weeks). Each course
may have
* lecture and tutorial component
*lecture and practicum component
*lecture, tutorial, and practicum component,
* only practicum component

         One credit for tutorial work means one hour of engagement per week. In a semester of
15 weeks’ duration, a one-credit tutorial in a course is equivalent to 15 hours of
engagement.
         A one-credit course in practicum or lab work, community engagement and services, and
fieldwork in a semester mean two-hour engagement per week. In a semester of 15
weeks’ duration, a one-credit practicum in a course is equivalent to 30 hours of
engagement.
         A one credit of Seminar or Internship or Studio activities or Field practice/ projects or
Community engagement and service means two-hour engagements per week.
Accordingly, in a semester of 15 weeks’ duration, one credit in these courses is
Equivalent to 30 hours of engagement.
         A course can have a combination of lecture credits, tutorial credits, and practicum
credits. For example, a 4-credit course with three credits assigned for lectures and one
credit for practicum shall have three 1-hour lectures per week and one 2-hour duration
field-based learning / project or lab work, or workshop activities per week.

In a semester of 15 weeks’ duration, a 4-credit course is equivalent to 45 hours of lectures
and 30 hours of practicum. Similarly, a 4 —credit course with 3- credits assigned for
lectures and one credit for tutorial shall have three 1-hour lectures per week and one 1-
hour tutorial per week. In a semester of 15 weeks’ duration, a four-credit course is
equivalent to 45 hours of lectures and 15 hours of tutorials

                            Maintenance of Discipline
       Great emphasis is laid on discipline and character building of students and they are
        expected to maintain a high standard of discipline.
       The students admitted to the college must abide by rules and regulations as prescribed
        by the college authority. Violation of rules, irregular attendance, irregular clearance of
        College and Hostel fees, showing disregard to the teachers and staff members in any
        form, adoption of unfair means during examination etc. are some of offences which may
        make students liable for disciplinary action.
       Student’s Union and all other Associations working in the College shall be subject to
        such guidance & control as the College administration may prescribe from time to time.
       Any notice desired to be pasted or circulated by the students anywhere in the College
        Premises shall require the approval of the Principal. The permission from the College
        Authority is required in order to conduct any activity in the campus.
       As per UGC Guideline no F 1-16/2007 (CPP-11) April 2009, all forms of Ragging in
        Hostels and outside and inside the college campus are prohibited. Ragging is considered
        as an offence under the law of the land and ragging in all its forms is totally banned in
        the entire institution.
       The courses of studies in the College are full time courses. No student can take any other
        full time course simultaneously.

    a) Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC):

As per revised NAAC guidance for quality up gradation of institution of higher education, the
Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) has been constituted with wide ranging powers. In order
to make a significant and meaningful contribution in the post accreditation phase, the IQAC
meets from time to time and makes plans to improve the overall quality of the college. For any
query, contact IQAC coordinator Dr. Karabi Goswami.

    b) Digital Learning Cell: As per UGC guidelines, a Digital learning cell has been set up
       in the College.
       Coordinator: Dr. Happy Saikia


    c) Grievance Redressal Cell:
                                                                                       P a g e | 13


A grievance redressal cell is working in the College to look into complaints of the students, staff
and guardians. Any complaint may be lodged in writing and dropped in the wooden box
installed near the Principal’s Chamber. Coordinator: Mr. Mrinal Jyoti Sarma.

    d) Career Guidance Cell and Counselling Cell:

There is a career guidance and counseling centre in the college. It not only gives information
about various employment schemes and competitive examinations but also organises coaching
programmes from time to time. For any query contact coordinator: Mr. Prithiraj Barkakoty.

    e) N.C.C. :

College has a NCC unit of 50 Cadets and unit is working under 8 Assam Bn. with an Associate
NCC officer(ANO). The Students are enrolled for obtaining “B” and “C” Certificates. Willing
students may contact the respective Prof. in-charge for enrolment- Lt. Balo Ram Nath.
    f) NSS:

College has an NSS Unit of 100 volunteers and a Programme Officer. Various socially relevant
services are provided by NSS students like blood donation camp, AIDS awareness rally, adult
education etc. Willing students may contact the respective Prof. in-charge for enrolment- Mr.
Parag Das.
    g) Cultural Activities:

    The College has carved out a special niche for itself in the field of extracurricular, extra
    mural activities. The College has been regularly participating in the youth festivals at
    Gauhati University. The students have been participating with full favour and zeal in all
    activities, academic, theatrical, or musical.

    h) Alumni Association:

    The Alumni Association provides a platform to the alumni of the college who can contribute
    immensely in the all- round development of their alma- matter.

    i)   Health and Hygiene:

    There is a First- Aid Health Care Centre in the Institution attached with NSS room.

    j)   Women Cell:

    There is a Women Cell in the College which conducts seminars and discussions on women’s
    issues. Any case relating to sexual harassment is dealt by the Cell and sent to management
    of the institution.

    k) Research & Development Cell: Coordinator: Dr. Pritilata Pegu
